name: STM8AF6223PDAU
title: STM8AF6213/13A/23/23A/26 automotive 8-bit microcontrollers: 4 to 8 Kbytes Flash, 640 bytes data EEPROM, 10-bit ADC, timers, LINUART, SPI, I2C, 3.0 to 5.5 V
summary: AEC-Q100 automotive 8-bit microcontrollers built on the STM8A core at up to 16 MHz, with 4 or 8 Kbytes of Flash, 640 bytes of data EEPROM and 1 Kbyte of RAM. They run from 3.0 V to 5.5 V at up to 150 °C ambient (D range), with internal 16 MHz and 128 kHz RC oscillators, a crystal oscillator, power-on and brown-out reset and two watchdogs. Peripherals are a 16-bit advanced control timer, a 16-bit and an 8-bit timer, a LIN 2.2 UART, SPI, I2C and a 10-bit ADC with up to 7 inputs. STM8AF6223PDAU is the 8-Kbyte, 7-input part in TSSOP20 for -40 °C to 150 °C, in tubes.
key_figures: 3.7 mA typ, 16 MHz HSI, code in Flash, 5 V
6.0 µA typ at 5 V, Flash powered down

Every device has TIM1 (multipurpose timer), TIM5 (PWM timer), TIM6 (8-bit timer), SPI, I2C, LINUART, window and independent watchdogs and the ADC.

tables.title: STM8AF6213/STM8AF6223 TSSOP20 pin description
rows: Top level interrupt [AFR3]; Timer 1 inverted channel 1 [AFR7]
notes: Port pins come out of reset as floating inputs; NRST has its pull-up, and PD1 is a pull-up input while reset is held and after it is released (4).
(1) I/Os that source or sink high current at the same time are to be spread evenly round the package, and the total current stays within the absolute maximum ratings.
(2) In Halt and Active-halt, PA1 becomes a weak pull-up input, does not drive its output and cannot wake the device; PA1 is best kept as an input when those modes are used.
(3) T: true open drain; the P-buffer, the weak pull-up and the protection diode to VDD are absent.
(4) PD1 is a pull-up input during reset and after the internal reset is released.
Speed codes: O1 is the 2 MHz slow output; O2 the 10 MHz fast output; O3 can be set either way and starts slow; O4 can be set either way and starts fast. HS marks a high-sink output.
[ ] marks an alternate function reached by an AFR option bit; once the remap is active the default alternate function is gone. A function listed twice in brackets is one choice between two places.
The PA2 output cells should read: high sink -, speed O1, OD X, PP X.
'Timer 52' in the PD2 and PD3 rows should read Timer 5.

tables.conditions: Absolute maximum ratings; voltages referred to VSS
rows: Input voltage on true open drain pins(2)
Input voltage on any other pin(2)
Variations between all the different ground pins
notes: Stress beyond these ratings can damage the device permanently; operation at them is not implied, and long exposure can reduce reliability. The mission profile follows JEDEC JESD47; extended profiles are available on request.
(1) Every VDD and VSS pin is to be connected to the external supply.

(2) IINJ(PIN) is never to be exceeded; keeping VIN within its maximum does this. Where VIN max cannot be kept, the injected current is to be limited externally to IINJ(PIN). VIN > VDD injects positive current, VIN < VSS negative. True open-drain pads have no positive injection, so their VIN max always applies.

tables.title: Current characteristics
tables.conditions: Absolute maximum ratings; max values guaranteed by characterization (1)
rows: Total current into VDD power lines (source)(2)
Total current out of VSS ground lines (sink)(2)
Output current sunk by any I/O and control pin
Output current source by any I/Os and control pin
Injected current on any other pin(5)
Total injected current (sum of all I/O and control pins)(5)
notes: (1) Guaranteed by characterization results.
(2) Every power pin (VDD, VDDIO, VDDA) and ground pin (VSS, VSSIO, VSSA) is to be connected to the external supply.
(3) As for VIN: staying within VIN max keeps IINJ(PIN) in range; otherwise the current is limited externally. True open-drain pads take no positive injection.

(4) Negative current injected into one analog input badly degrades the conversion running on another; a Schottky diode from such a pin to ground is recommended. Positive injection within IINJ(PIN) and ∑IINJ(PIN) leaves ADC accuracy unchanged.
(5) When several pins take injected current together, ∑IINJ(PIN) adds the magnitudes of the instantaneous positive and negative currents; characterized with the full total spread over four I/O pins.

circuits.title: VCAP external capacitor
circuits.description: The core regulator output VCAP is stabilised by one external capacitor CEXT to ground, 470 nF to 3300 nF with ESR up to 0.3 Ω and ESL up to 15 nH at 1 MHz. The capacitor's tolerance and its drift with temperature, DC bias and frequency have to stay inside those limits.

circuits.title: HSE external clock source
circuits.description: An external clock of up to 16 MHz drives OSCIN directly, with levels between VHSEL and VHSEH; the EXTCLK option bit selects this mode.

circuits.title: HSE crystal or ceramic resonator oscillator
circuits.description: A 1 MHz to 16 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator sits between OSCIN and OSCOUT, with a load capacitor from each pin to ground (CL1 = CL2 = C, up to 20 pF, about twice the crystal's CLOAD). Inside, a transconductance stage with a 220 kΩ feedback resistor drives the resonator. Resonator and capacitors belong right next to the two pins.
notes: The crystal is to satisfy gm ≫ gmcrit (see the gmcrit equation).

circuits.title: Recommended reset pin protection
circuits.description: A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground guards against parasitic resets; an optional external reset circuit shares the node. The internal pull-up RPU charges the capacitor. Whatever drives NRST has to be able to pull it below VIL(NRST) max.
notes: A smaller capacitor lowers the charge and discharge current where power matters.
If NRST also resets other circuits, the capacitor's charge and discharge time sets the reset timing those circuits see.

operation.text: Five automotive 8-bit parts form one family: STM8AF6213 and STM8AF6213A (4 Kbytes Flash), STM8AF6223 and STM8AF6223A (8 Kbytes) in TSSOP20, and STM8AF6226 (8 Kbytes) in LQFP32 or VFQFPN32. All have 640 bytes of true data EEPROM rated for 300 k write/erase cycles, 1 Kbyte RAM, internal oscillators, watchdogs and brown-out reset. In TSSOP20 the A versions have 7 ADC channels, 6 timer capture/compare channels and 2 complementary outputs, the others 5, 7 and 1. RM0016 calls this group low-density and holds the register detail; PM0051 covers Flash programming, UM0470 SWIM and debug, PM0044 the core.

STM8 core, Harvard architecture with a 3-stage pipeline and a 32-bit program bus that fetches most instructions in one cycle. Registers: 8-bit accumulator, 16-bit X and Y index registers, 24-bit program counter (16 Mbyte linear space), 16-bit stack pointer (64 Kbyte stack), 8-bit condition code register with 7 flags. 20 addressing modes, including indexed indirect and stack-pointer relative; 80 instructions averaging 2 bytes, with 8 × 8 multiply, 16 / 8 and 16 / 16 divide, bit operations and direct memory-to-memory moves.

A single-wire interface on PD1 (SWIM) gives access to debug mode and memory programming in every operating mode, at up to 145 bytes/ms. The debug module reads and writes RAM and peripheral registers on the fly, reaches every resource by stalling the CPU, sets software breakpoints on any instruction and offers two advanced breakpoints with 23 predefined configurations; shadow registers show CPU state in real time.

Nested interrupt controller with three software priority levels, 32 vectors with hardware priority, up to 28 external interrupt lines on 7 vectors including the top level interrupt TLI, plus trap and reset.

operation.topic: Flash, data EEPROM and write protection
operation.text: Up to 8 Kbytes of single-supply Flash, 640 bytes of data EEPROM and an option byte area. The memory access security system (MASS) always write-protects Flash, data EEPROM and option bytes; application code unlocks it with a key sequence written to a control register for in-application programming. A second level, the user boot code area (UBC), covers from one 64-byte page up to the whole 8 Kbytes, set in page steps by the UBC option byte in ICP mode; MASS keys do not unlock it, so it can hold the boot code, vectors, reset routine and IAP routines. The data EEPROM has no read-while-write.
With ROP set (OPT0 = 0xAA), the Flash and data EEPROM cannot be read or written through ICP or debug. Changing the ROP state erases program and data memory.

Four sources can drive fMASTER: a 1 MHz to 16 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator (HSE), an external clock up to 16 MHz on OSCIN, the 16 MHz internal RC (HSI) and the 128 kHz internal RC (LSI). A programmable prescaler sets the CPU and peripheral clock; sources switch on the fly without glitches, the switch waiting until the new source is ready. Clocks to the core, each peripheral (CLK_PCKENR1/2) and memory can be gated off. After reset the device runs from HSI/8, 2 MHz. The clock security system, when enabled, falls back to HSI/8 on an HSE failure and can raise an interrupt. A configurable clock output (CLK_CCO) brings a clock out to a pin.

Wait: the CPU stops, peripherals run; any interrupt or reset wakes it. Active-halt with the main regulator on: CPU and peripheral clocks stop, the auto-wakeup unit wakes the device at programmed intervals; faster wakeup, higher current. Active-halt with the regulator off: the same with lower current and slower wakeup. Halt: clocks and main regulator off, lowest current; an external event or reset wakes it. REGAH in CLK_ICKR picks the regulator state and AHALT in FLASH_CR1 the Flash mode in Active-halt.

Two independent watchdogs, each enabled by option byte or by software; once running neither can be stopped without a reset. The window watchdog resets the device on timeout, adjustable from 75 µs to 64 ms at a 16 MHz CPU clock, and also when it is refreshed before its count falls below the window register value. The independent watchdog runs from the 128 kHz LSI, so it keeps working if the CPU clock fails; its time base covers 60 µs to 1 s.

The auto-wakeup counter brings the device out of Active-halt, clocked by the LSI or by the HSE through a prescaler (CKAWUSEL, PRSC option bits); the LSI can also be routed to TIM1 input capture channel 1 to calibrate it. The beeper drives the BEEP pin at 1, 2 or 4 kHz; its output port is reached through the AFR7 remap option bit.

16-bit advanced control timer counting up, down or up/down with a 16-bit prescaler, four capture/compare channels (input capture, output compare, edge- or centre-aligned PWM, one-pulse), three complementary outputs with programmable dead time, a break input that forces the outputs to a set state, encoder mode and synchronization with external signals or with TIM5 and TIM6. Suited to motor control, lighting and half-bridge drive.

TIM5: 16-bit up-counting auto-reload timer, prescaler in powers of 2 from 1 to 32768, three capture/compare channels, PWM, synchronization with TIM1 or TIM6. TIM6: 8-bit auto-reload basic timer clocked by the CPU clock, prescaler in powers of 2 from 1 to 128, one update interrupt, synchronization with TIM1 or TIM5.

10-bit successive-approximation ADC with up to 7 external inputs and one internal one, input range 0 to VDD, 14 ADC clocks per conversion. Single, continuous and buffered continuous modes, a result buffer of one 10-bit word per channel, scan of a channel sequence, an analog watchdog with upper and lower thresholds and its interrupt, end-of-conversion interrupt, external trigger and TIM1 TRGO trigger. AIN7 is wired to the internal bandgap reference, which does not move with VDD or TA and can be used to measure VDD. AIN12 cannot be used in scan mode or with the analog watchdog; its result goes only to ADC_DRH/ADC_DRL.

Called UART4 in RM0016. Full-duplex asynchronous UART up to 1 Mbit/s (fCPU/16) with a fractional baud rate generator, separate transmitter and receiver enables, address-bit and idle-line wakeup, parity and error interrupts; synchronous SPI-master mode up to 1 Mbit/s at 16 MHz; smartcard and IrDA SIR modes; single-wire half duplex; LIN 2.2. As LIN master it generates break and delimiter and detects them with its own flag; as LIN slave it handles headers on its own with one interrupt per valid header, mutes unwanted responses, checks identifier parity, resynchronises automatically so the HSI can be its clock, detects breaks at any time and flags short delimiters, synch-field and deviation errors, framing errors and header timeouts.

Up to 8 Mbit/s (fMASTER/2) as master or slave, full duplex or simplex on two lines with a bidirectional data line option, master/slave selected by hardware or software, CRC, one-byte transmit and receive buffers and a slave-select input.

Master (clock, start and stop generation) and slave (programmable address, stop detection) with 7- and 10-bit addressing and general call, at standard speed up to 100 kHz and fast speed up to 400 kHz. fMASTER must be 8 MHz or more for 400 kHz.

Every port pin is a CMOS input with optional weak pull-up (about 55 kΩ) and external interrupt, and an open-drain or push-pull output; most can sink high current (HS). PB4 and PB5 are true open-drain: no P-channel driver, pull-up or diode to VDD, and their absolute maximum input is 6.5 V instead of VDD + 0.3 V. Output speed is fixed slow (O1, 2 MHz), fixed fast (O2, 10 MHz), or programmable starting slow (O3) or fast (O4). After reset the pins are floating inputs; PD1 (SWIM) is a pull-up input during and after reset. Unused pins are to be tied to a fixed level, as outputs or through external resistors. High-current pins used together are to be spread evenly round the package.
In Halt and Active-halt, PA1/OSCIN turns into a weak pull-up input with its output undriven, and it cannot wake the device; PA1 is best used only as an input in designs that use those modes.

Eight AFR option bits in OPT2 move alternate functions to other pins; when a remap is on, the default alternate function on that pin is gone, and only one remap option should be used per port. The peripheral still has to be enabled in its own registers, and remapping does not change the GPIO behaviour of the pins. With AFR1 and AFR0 both set, the SPI loses hardware NSS and needs SSM set in SPI_CR2.

Option bytes hold hardware configuration and memory protection. Each one except ROP is stored twice, plain (OPTx) and complemented (NOPTx). They are written in ICP mode over SWIM at their EEPROM addresses, or by the application in IAP mode, except ROP and UBC which only ICP can change.

A 96-bit identifier, fixed at manufacture, holds the wafer X and Y coordinates, wafer number and lot number at 0x4865 to 0x4870. It is read byte by byte and can serve as a serial number, as a key ingredient for code security and for secure boot.

Voltages are referred to VSS. Min and max values hold over the worst ambient temperature, supply voltage and frequency and are production-tested on every part at TA = -40 °C, 25 °C and TAmax, unless a footnote marks them as characterization, simulation or design values. Typical values are at TA = 25 °C and VDD = 5.0 V and are not tested; typical ADC accuracy is characterized on samples from one standard diffusion lot across temperature. Typical curves serve as design guidance only and are not tested.

The power-on reset releases at VIT+ (2.7 V typ) and the brown-out reset trips at VIT- (2.65 V typ), with 70 mV hysteresis; reset is released 1.7 ms max after VDD rises. A reset always comes after a tTEMP delay, so VDD has to remain above VDD min when tTEMP ends. The VDD rise and fall rates are 2 µs/V or slower. Up to 16 MHz is available over the whole 3.0 V to 5.5 V range at TA -40 °C to 150 °C.

The crystal oscillator runs at 1 MHz to 16 MHz with a 220 kΩ internal feedback resistor and 5 mA/V minimum transconductance, and takes about 1 ms to start with a stabilised VDD. Load capacitors are up to 20 pF each. It draws 6 mA while starting and 1.2 mA to 1.6 mA once stable. HSECNT in OPT5 sets the stabilisation wait from 0.5 to 2048 HSE cycles. A resonator with low Rm lowers the supply current.

Factory-calibrated HSI accuracy is ±5% over -40 °C to 150 °C, or ±3% to 125 °C for the I order codes (STM8AF62xxIxx). The application can trim it to ±1% with the 3-bit calibration or ±0.5% with the 4-bit calibration enabled by the HSITRIM option bit.

Writing and erasing work from -40 °C to 150 °C. Program Flash: 1000 cycles, retention 40 years at 25 °C or 20 years at 55 °C. Data EEPROM: 300 k cycles at 25 °C, 100 k from -40 °C to 125 °C, retention 40 years at 25 °C or 20 years at 55 °C (for 256 bytes after up to 1000 cycles at 125 °C). Cycling counts in 4-byte words. Code runs down to 2.6 V; writing and erasing need 3.0 V.

Each pin takes up to ±4 mA of injected current and all pins together ±20 mA; respecting VIN limits keeps within them, otherwise the current must be limited externally. True open-drain pins accept no positive injection. Negative injection on any analog input degrades conversions on the others; a Schottky diode from such pins to ground is recommended.

NRST is a bidirectional reset with a 30 kΩ to 80 kΩ internal pull-up; pulses under 75 ns are filtered, pulses over 500 ns are taken, and internal resets drive it low for at least 20 µs. A 0.1 µF capacitor to ground (100 nF minimum recommended) protects against parasitic resets; a smaller value lowers the charge current where power matters.

ET, total unadjusted error: the largest gap between the real and ideal transfer curves. EO, offset error: the gap between the first real and first ideal transitions. EG, gain error: the gap between the last ideal and last real transitions. ED, differential linearity error: the largest difference between a real step and the ideal step. EL, integral linearity error: the largest gap between a real transition and the line through the end points.

Susceptibility is characterized on samples running a two-LED toggle program: ESD on every pin to IEC 61000-4-2 and fast transient bursts through 100 pF on VDD and VSS to IEC 61000-4-4, until a disturbance; a reset restores normal running. Emission is measured to IEC 61967-2. Unexpected resets and program-counter corruption can mostly be recovered by holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 s; AN1015 covers software hardening.

The order code sets the temperature range. Example: TAmax 75 °C, IDDmax 8 mA at VDD 5 V, 20 outputs low at IOL 8 mA and VOL 0.4 V. PINTmax is taken as 400 mW and PIOmax as 20 × 8 mA × 0.4 V = 64 mW, so PDmax = 464 mW; in LQFP32 (60 °C/W) TJmax = 75 °C + 27.8 °C = 102.8 °C, which calls for at least the C (125 °C) range. PINTmax = 8 mA × 5 V should read 40 mW.

The top side carries the ST logo, product identification, a date code (year Y, week WW) and a revision code, with the pin 1 mark. Parts marked ES or E are engineering samples, not qualified for production use.

Supported by the STice emulator and low-cost in-circuit debugger/programmers over SWIM, the free STM8 toolset (STVD IDE and STVP programmer), Cosmic, Raisonance and IAR C compilers and the STM8 assembler/linker, and third-party gang programmers.
